item.text: {"question_id":"4B.1","answer":"In 2023, Mexico retained meaningful electoral contestability, but the supplied evidence does not show López Obrador supporting or voluntarily self-binding to the institutional conditions that made it possible. The INE and courts preserved the prior electoral framework, and the June local elections were reported as successful and transparent; these are outcomes of institutional resistance and inherited arrangements, not evidence of presidential support. Against this, López Obrador backed Plan B, which would have reduced INE funding, staffing, professional and local capacity, enforcement powers, fiscal oversight, voter-registration safeguards, and affirmative-action protections. The reforms were suspended and invalidated by the Supreme Court, so the documented risks were not fully implemented, but that correction limits attribution of harm rather than establishing presidential acceptance of contestability. The 2023 Morena succession process also involved extensive public-space advertising and avoidance of the normal fiscalization process, while analysis described López Obrador as seeking continuing influence over the next administration; the supplied evidence does not prove he personally ordered every expenditure or that the process determined the election. No verified 2023 opposition victory or direct evidence of López Obrador accepting such a victory is supplied. Overall, contestability remained operational during the period, but ruler-attributable support was mixed and materially undermined by attempts to weaken electoral administration and shape
